## What it is

An interactive web app that opens Mplus `.dgm` diagram files and `.out` output files and draws them as editable path diagrams.

- Runs entirely in the browser: nothing leaves the browser.
- Live: <https://amelia-m.github.io/mplusplus/>
- Source: <https://github.com/amelia-m/mplusplus> (LGPL-3.0-or-later)
- Independent: not affiliated with or endorsed by Muthén & Muthén.

::: notes
Demo here if time allows: open a demo example from the drop zone.
:::

## Why

- Mplus's Diagrammer draws the model, but its labels collide.
- The goal: match Mplus's diagrams as a minimum (a "parity mode", still to come), then improve on them.
- Things it adds today: label collision avoidance, residuals on the outer edge, rotate and flip, undo, autosave, export with provenance.

## What it does {.smaller}

- Parses `.dgm` and `.out` files, tolerant of header drift.
- Lays out the model following Mplus's own columns (the `.dgm`'s level line), with indicators fanned out and straight paths.
- Drag, select, align, rotate, flip, zoom and pan.
- Styles by significance, sign and size, with an inspector for overrides.
- Exports SVG, PNG and PDF, each recording the source file and its hash.

## The format nobody documents {.smaller}

- A `.dgm` file is Mplus syntax, a line `INPUT_END`, then a table of numbers.
- The estimate codes are not publicly documented, so their meaning was inferred from the corpus.
  - Last digit: parameter type (loading or regression, covariance, residual variance, variance).
  - Tens digit: unstandardized, STDYX, STDY, STD, or a constraint label.
- A header line gives each non-indicator variable's column: inferred from 49 files and 11 diagrams, Mplus 8.11 only.
- Test fixtures are synthetic models simulated and fitted with Mplus, plus a few openly licensed published ones.

## How it was built {.smaller}

- Designed by me; implemented with Claude Code (Anthropic).
- I make the decisions; the agent proposes, builds, tests and reviews.
- My working rules for the agent:
  - A task contract (scope, non-goals, acceptance) before any agent is dispatched.
  - A local code review before every push; every merge waits for me.
  - Every drawing and layout decision recorded with its source, who decided it and when.

## Decisions have sources

- `docs/diagram-conventions.md` logs every drawing and layout rule: 19 decisions.
- Each one says its evidence level: stated, shown, observed, inferred or a choice.
- A source counts only if its own text or figure was read, not a search summary.
- Example: covariances are solid curves with two arrowheads (Kline; Raykov and Marcoulides; Mplus's own output).

## What went sideways {.smaller}

- **Autosave across tabs**: with one shared slot, four review rounds kept finding ways a tab could lose its diagram; replaced with one slot per tab.
- **The second layout engine**: ELK was EPL-2.0 only, which does not combine with the LGPL, and was most of the bundle.
  Dropped: the built app went from 1,530 kB to 92 kB.
- **Undocumented formats**: every meaning inferred from files gets labeled as inferred, so it can be revisited.

## What is next

- Parity mode: show on any diagram that the output matches Mplus.
- Reading Mplus's own saved diagrams (`.mdg`) for exact positions to test against.
- More output types: categorical, Bayesian, Mplus 9, then multilevel and mixture.
- Saving diagrams as `.dgm` and as an app file that keeps edits.
